chapter_title: Elucidating the Role of Biliverdin Reductase in the Expression of Heme Oxygenase-1 as a Cytoprotective Response to Stress
source_pdf: /mnt/project-files/Experimental Provenance for QSAR Dataset/Pharmacology (Luca Gallelli) (z-library.sk, 1lib.sk, z-lib.sk).pdf

records.mechanism_book_wording: activate guanylyl cyclase
records.quote: the CO formed by HO-1 has been shown to activate guanylyl cyclase to mediate the relaxation and dilation responses
records.notes: CO is the product of the HO-1 reaction. Target class (enzyme) is my inference; the page names only guanylyl cyclase.

records.role_detail: partial agonist (book's word); book says it may down-regulate NOS-dependent signaling
records.mechanism_book_wording: serve as a partial agonist of nitric oxide synthetase (NOS) and thus, may down-regulate the level of NOS-dependent signaling
records.quote: CO has been shown to serve as a partial agonist to nitric oxide synthetase (NOS) and thus, may down-regulate the level of NOS-dependent signaling
records.quote_corrected_reading: CO has been shown to serve as a partial agonist of nitric oxide synthetase (NOS) and thus, may down-regulate the level of NOS-dependent signaling
records.notes: Book calls CO a partial agonist of an enzyme. Role Inhibitor in the rule name is my inference from the book's 'down-regulate'; Activator is the alternative reading of 'partial agonist'.

records.mechanism_book_wording: activate the P38 MAPK pathway
records.quote: the ability of CO (and CO-releasing molecules) to activate the P38 MAPK pathway
records.notes: Page names a pathway; p38 MAPK is a kinase, so the enzyme class is my inference. Page 567 says CO activates P38 but inhibits JNK/ERK MAPKs.

records.mechanism_book_wording: dramatically inhibited JNK MAPK signaling
records.quote: CO dramatically inhibited JNK MAPK signaling in murine macrophages exposed to endotoxin
records.notes: Statement is about signaling in macrophages; JNK is a kinase, so the enzyme class is my inference.

records.role_detail: effect reported in human airway smooth muscle cells, via guanylyl cyclase
records.mechanism_book_wording: led to inhibition of ERK1/2 MAPK
records.quote: CO-mediated affects on guanylyl cyclase led to inhibition of ERK1/2 MAPK
records.notes: ERK is a kinase, so the enzyme class is my inference.

records.target: complex III of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (terminal step of oxidative phosphorylation)
records.mechanism_book_wording: a potent inhibitor of the complex III-mediated terminal step of oxidative phosphorylation
records.quote: CO is a potent inhibitor of the complex III-mediated terminal step of oxidative phosphorylation
records.notes: Enzyme class is my inference (complex III is an enzyme complex); the page does not call it an enzyme.

records.mechanism_book_wording: The ability of the molecule to inhibit cyclooxygenase
records.quote: The ability of the molecule to inhibit cyclooxygenase may provide an anti-inflammatory effect
records.notes: 'The molecule' refers to CO in the preceding sentences (CO released from HO-1).

records.mechanism_book_wording: CO also inhibits cytochromes P450
records.quote: CO also inhibits cytochromes P450
records.notes: Page 550 (printed 538) says CO has been postulated to inhibit P450 enzymes because the ferrous heme protein forms a tight-binding complex with CO.

records.drug_kind: endogenous enzyme acting on another enzyme (not a compound)
records.target: P450 activity (via competition for P450 reductase)
records.role_detail: indirect inhibition, by competing for P450 reductase
records.mechanism_book_wording: indirectly inhibiting P450 activity
records.quote: HO-1 may provide cytoprotection by indirectly inhibiting P450 activity
records.notes: Book frames this as a hypothesis ('far from proven'). The actor is the enzyme HO-1, not a drug.

records.mechanism_book_wording: a potent inhibitor of c-Jun N-terminal kinase and AP-1 pathway
records.quote: Biliverdin has also been shown to be a potent inhibitor of c-Jun N-terminal kinase and AP-1 pathway
records.notes: Page 567 says 'biliverdin has been shown to be a potent inhibitor of JNK MAPK'.

records.mechanism_book_wording: activate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor
records.quote: both biliverdin and bilirubin activate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor to induce expression of a spectrum of genes
records.notes: 'Agonist' is my reading of 'activate' on a receptor.

records.mechanism_book_wording: activate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor
records.quote: both biliverdin and bilirubin activate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor to induce expression of a spectrum of genes
records.notes: Same sentence as the biliverdin record. 'Agonist' is my reading of 'activate' on a receptor.

records.mechanism_book_wording: bilirubin also inhibits the superoxide-generating NADPH oxidase
records.quote: bilirubin also inhibits the superoxide-generating NADPH oxidase

records.mechanism_book_wording: acts as an inhibitor of HO-1
records.quote: chromium mesoporphyrin, which acts as an inhibitor of HO-1

records.mechanism_book_wording: an inhibitor of HO-1
records.quote: treatment with tin mesoporphyrin, an inhibitor of HO-1, did not prevent renal injury
records.notes: Page 568 says HO-1 'activity was inhibited by treatment with tin mesoporphyrin'. Page 553 also mentions stannic mesoporphyrin abolishing HO-1 protection, without stating its mechanism.

records.mechanism_book_wording: to inhibit HO-1 activity
records.quote: treated with tin porphyrin 1 hour before administration of carbon tetrachloride to inhibit HO-1 activity
records.numbers_detail: timing only: 1 hour before carbon tetrachloride (PDF page 552); no dose amount given

records.mechanism_book_wording: bind to the HO active site resulting in the inhibition of enzyme activity
records.quote: the metal porphyrins will often bind to the HO active site resulting in the inhibition of enzyme activity
records.notes: Class statement. Zinc mesoporphyrin is named on the same page (quercetin effects abrogated by it) and page 552 says 'metal porphyrins that inhibited the HO-1 activity', but the page does not state zinc mesoporphyrin's mechanism on its own, so no separate record.

records.drug_kind: endogenous enzyme acting on another enzyme (not a compound)
records.mechanism_book_wording: can activate two protein kinase C proteins, βII and ζ
records.quote: Phosphorylated BVR can activate two protein kinase C proteins, βII and ζ
records.notes: The actor is a protein (BVR), not a drug. Page 561 also says PKC betaII can in turn activate BVR.

records.drug_kind: endogenous enzyme acting on another enzyme (not a compound)
records.mechanism_book_wording: can activate two protein kinase C proteins, βII and ζ
records.quote: Phosphorylated BVR can activate two protein kinase C proteins, βII and ζ
records.notes: Same sentence as the betaII record. The actor is a protein (BVR), not a drug.

records.drug_kind: endogenous enzyme acting on another enzyme (not a compound)
records.mechanism_book_wording: has been shown to activate ERK MAPK
records.quote: BVR has been shown to activate ERK MAPK
records.notes: The actor is a protein (BVR), not a drug. ERK is a kinase, so the enzyme class is my inference.

chapter_notes: Review chapter on HO-1/BVR cytoprotection; no drug potencies or other numbers are given for any mechanism. Skipped 4 statements whose target is neither receptor nor enzyme (CO activating calcium-dependent potassium channels, biliverdin inhibiting NF-kB, Bach-1 blocking Nrf2 binding, Keap-1/Nrf2 regulation); transcription-factor interactions were not counted systematically. Hemin, quercetin and tin chloride are described only as inducers of HO-1 expression, so no records were written for them. All 34 pages (547-580) were viewed, including the reference list, which starts on PDF page 570 after the Conclusions.
